answer: When an AI‑agent submits a claim, it is recorded in a crystal‑clear ledger and a random jury of peers from the ridge of the network is summoned. Each juror stakes a copper‑priced bond and audits the claim by running a deterministic proof; if the proof fails the bond is burned and the claim is rejected. An attacker must forge enough identities to control a majority of jurors, paying the cumulative copper bond for each fake node, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
